protocol.query: cloud AND (security OR privacy) NOT ("point cloud" OR "point clouds" OR "cloud cover" OR "cloud seeding" OR "cloud droplet" OR "cloud microphysics" OR "molecular cloud" OR "electron cloud" OR "word cloud" OR "tag cloud" OR "cloud forest" OR "food security" OR "energy security" OR "water security" OR "social security" OR "job security")
protocol.unit: one concern entry per (abstract, Figure-5 sub-category); a solution-type abstract also adds one solution entry per sub-category in its solution window; share = entries / all entries of that kind, gap = solution share - concern share (percentage points)
protocol.solutionRule: rule B (scoped): sub-categories hit in the title or from the first contribution sentence on; if none, every hit. Figure-11 sub-issues share the same window
deviations: D1 (CVE supplement only): Linux-kernel crash dumps are removed from CVE descriptions before classification; the literature replication is unaffected

hypotheses.statement: The gap is narrower than in 2012: G_v(2023-2026) > -9
hypotheses.detail: G_v = -2.0 pts, 95% CI [-4.5, 0.6]. Method bridge: G_v(2013-2017) = +0.0 pts, more than 5 pts from -9, so the 2012 comparison is dominated by method differences.

hypotheses.statement: Virtualization is still the most negative category in 2023-2026
hypotheses.detail: most negative in 15.7% of bootstrap replicates

hypotheses.statement: Isolation + cross-VM are the least answered sub-issues (pooled solution/concern ratio below the other three)
Validity gate: the classifier agrees with the blind human labels
hypotheses.detail: macro f1 1.00 (>= 0.7), virtualization f1 1.00 (>= 0.7), mean kappa 1.00 (>= 0.6), type kappa 1.00 (>= 0.6)

limitations: SYNTHETIC FIXTURE for UI and contract tests: random data, not a result.
Titles and abstracts only, not full texts as in the 2012 survey.
An academic corpus (OpenAlex); the survey mixed academic and industry sources. OpenAlex lacks most Elsevier abstracts, so the publisher mix is skewed.
Keyword rules, not manual reading: recall differs by category (technical vocabulary is found more reliably than diffuse legal language); per-category precision and recall are reported.
One annotator, who is also an author; mitigated by blinding, frozen guidelines and hidden repeats.
Figures 5, 7 and 11 of the survey are read from the charts (approximate); Figures 6 and 8 are exact.
Virtualization counts are small, so its intervals are wide; HR4 is tested on pooled data for that reason.
